newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary to extend import duty preferences in July.
newsitem.headline: Hungary to extend import duty preferences in July.

text.p: Hungary will increase preferential customs duties on goods from 28 European countries from July 1 but the measure will not affect the trade account, the Finance Ministry said on Wednesday.

Under the "pan-European" agreement signed by 29 countries, raw and semi-processed materials from the region used in production will add to customs preferences on goods from the signing countries, the ministry said in a statement.
The signers of the agreement were the European Union, European Free Trade Agreement and Central European Free Trade Agreement members, Bulgaria, Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania, it said.
Department Head Sara Beszteri said the agreement took effect in most of the member countries earlier this year.
She added that Hungary's lining up would not increase the trade gap.
"Certainly there will not be substantial change (in the trade account)," she told Reuters.

The agreement will be unfavourable for those companies which import raw and semi-processed materials from the CIS countries and positive for those who import these materials from the "pan-European region", she told a news conference.
This was likely to encourage these companies to restructure their imports, she said, adding that two-thirds of Hungary's imported raw materials came from the members of the agreement.
She added that the agreement was likely to encourage investors from outside the pan-European region, including Japanese companies, to increase their semi-processed material production in the region.
Beszteri said that Hungary began negotiations on free trade agreements with the Baltic countries and Bulgaria and the talks were likely to be concluded within this year.
